## Body

Grade delivery guard outcomes separately from cache-state predictions. A cache-view cold/unknown result does not mean a send was refused or warned: the guard ignores small seats. In #256 R256-001, substituting cache-view metrics for guard outcomes produced misleading headlines. Keep guard_* and cache_* columns separate, and count Warn alongside refusal when measuring warm-seat friction (harness/scripts/cache-ttl-audit.py:186-192,255-283 at d94fa60ff4a214f6101987a64939e1e361d17c85).

An intentional Warn is an ordinary allowed delivery with a warning receipt, not a forced Cold override. Under the reviewed default it warns past TTL through the hour; past the hour remains Cold. Absence of a forced-wake event for Warn is therefore not an audit bypass. For an actual forced Cold, verify nonempty reason validation occurs before the verdict and successful audit publication before delivery; publication failure must refuse (crates/core/src/cold_wake.rs:263-284; crates/daemon/src/http/cold_wake.rs:185-195,211-264). Recheck these boundaries when changing the switch, not just its default value.

Final #256 security evidence is output commit a64ffed08979d9923b228eaefe324d002b59802e, pass-with-notes at the head above. Source inspection plus exact-head CI/finality only; no local tests or live audit. PM explicitly assigned f214-audit-after to PERFORMANCE ONLY, superseding the round-1 security-owned debt: do not run a duplicate security audit. Existing usage-extraction, public-scrub and delegated-evidence notes cover the other lessons; they are not repeated here.
